clue.text: Making half-hearted effort like 'Doctor' McKeith

definitions.meaning: doing something mechanically, without real commitment, is a set idiom for a feeble effort
Gillian McKeith, the TV nutritionist, examined people's stools on screen; motions are bowel movements, so she literally sifted through them

explanation.surface: A jibe that a celebrity health guru, styled 'Doctor', puts in only token effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Gillian McKeith fronted the British TV show You Are What You Eat, famously inspecting participants' faeces; 'motions' is a polite word for stools.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes performing actions perfunctorily, with no genuine enthusiasm behind them.

clue.text: Imagined Queen always protected by a lot of money

indicators.note: something protected by another sits inside it, so one word encloses the other
a lot of, not all, so the final letter of the coin word is dropped

parts.note: a guinea is an old British gold coin, worth 21 shillings
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a royal whose fortune is guarded by a great heap of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the coin's last letter before 'protected by' wraps it round the word for always. A guinea is an old British coin worth 21 shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's consort in the legends is a queen of fiction rather than history, hence imagined.

clue.text: Can current politician overturn polite refusal

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: in a down clue overturning turns the polite-refusal words upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: no sir is a courteous way to refuse

explanation.surface: Can a sitting politician reverse a courteous no?
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturn' turns NO SIR into RISON. 'Can' looks like the start of a question but is the verb meaning to lock up.
explanation.definitionFit: To can someone is slang for putting them in jail, a synonym for locking up.

clue.text: Clearing youngster in case of genocide

indicators.note: in places the youngster inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A youth caught up in a genocide trial is cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearing in a wood, an open space among trees, is a synonym.

clue.text: Unlucky Romeo's conned over minor punishment

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
Romeo's reads as Romeo is held, so the letter for Romeo goes inside the word for conned

parts.note: to be had is to be conned
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lines are a school punishment of writing a sentence many times

explanation.surface: Bad luck: a Romeo was duped and gets only a slap on the wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside HAD. Lines, writing out a sentence over and over, are a traditional British school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The British exclamation of sympathy for bad luck is a synonym for unlucky.

clue.text: Study endlessly to get through exam — not a nice experience

indicators.note: one piece getting through another passes inside it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the word for study

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for working

explanation.surface: Cramming nonstop to pass a test is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' suggests revision, but here it is a room, and 'endlessly' docks its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trying, painful experience is a synonym for a hard test of endurance.

clue.text: 'Wind essentially' — diagnosis from old doctor

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter, of diagnosis

explanation.surface: An ancient physician diagnoses a patient with flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the middle letter of the nine-letter 'diagnosis', N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek physician of the 2nd century AD was a celebrated doctor of antiquity.

clue.text: One spotted by chance turning green

indicators.note: by means beside, so the reversed green word sits next to the chance word
turning reads the word for green backwards

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, green
lot means chance, as in leaving it to lot

explanation.surface: Someone happens to be noticed going green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes ECO into OCE. 'Spotted' looks like seen, but the cat has a spotted coat.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild cat of the Americas has a dappled coat, so it is one with spots.

clue.text: Exhausted duke finally in American party

indicators.note: in puts the duke's last letter inside the run of the other two pieces

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of duke

explanation.surface: A nobleman worn out after an American party.
explanation.walkthrough: The party is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, not an American one; 'finally' picks the duke's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely consumed or spent is a synonym for worn out.

clue.text: My relative put money across counter? On the contrary

indicators.note: put across means one piece spans the other, enclosing it
on the contrary reverses which piece wraps which, so the counter goes across the money

parts.note: a chip is a counter used in gambling

explanation.surface: A shopper hands cash over the till, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' swaps the roles: CHIP goes across M, not M across CHIP. The 'My' is the setter speaking as a human, a cousin of apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans and this great ape share a recent common ancestor, so it is a close relative of the setter.

clue.text: Terriers at peak fitness on manoeuvres — leader succeeded

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or in top condition, written with the 1 as letter I

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters of leader are rearranged

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Dogs in top condition on an exercise, with the pack leader taking over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on manoeuvres' rearranges LEADER into REDALE. A1, meaning first-class, is used with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Yorkshire breed, named after a river valley, is the biggest of the terriers.

clue.text: Wind up here? No, grounds extensive but there's no women

parts.note: lees are dregs, the grounds settling in a drink

indicators.note: there's no women says the letter for women is removed

parts.note: wide means extensive

explanation.surface: Someone surveys broad estate grounds and finds no women about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no' takes W out of WIDE, leaving IDE. The definition plays on the sheltered side being where the wind is not.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side, away from the wind, is where the wind does not blow up.

clue.text: At last! Nigel got found out

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of Nigel

parts.note: earned means got, as wages

explanation.surface: Finally Nigel has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last!' looks like an exclamation of relief but picks the last letter of Nigel.
explanation.definitionFit: To have discovered a fact is a synonym for having come to know it.

clue.text: See 1
Trouble in store broadcasting inside China

indicators.note: inside places the broadcasting word within the rearranged letters
to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of in store are disturbed

parts.note: on air means broadcasting, so on

explanation.surface: A disturbance at a shop while a programme from China airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' rearranges IN STORE into IRSTONE, and 'inside' puts ON within it.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard white earthenware is a type of china, crockery made in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Shut up shop

definitions.meaning: to confine in a small pen, as hens are
a co-operative society store, a familiar British chain

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper closes for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British chain of co-operative stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Confining birds in a pen is one sense; the cooperative grocer is the other.

clue.text: One able to run with leaders of government and security forces

indicators.note: a run of letters, like a ladder in a stocking, rearranges them in this clue

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone capable runs with the government and security forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' rearranges I, ABLE TO, G and S; 'able to' looks like a phrase but 'to' is fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind or compel someone to act is a synonym for constraining them.

clue.text: Meat! Gone to stuff myself

parts.note: past means gone
to ram is to stuff or cram
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Someone sees cold cuts and resolves to gorge on them.
explanation.definitionFit: This smoked, spiced cured beef is a deli meat.

clue.text: Crown Prince following American has-been

indicators.note: following places the prince's letter after the American one

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, a has-been

explanation.surface: A royal heir trails a washed-up American celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests royalty with the Prince, but it means the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a hill or head is its top, highest point.

clue.text: Offer not a sausage over, getting cross

indicators.note: over turns the letters back to front in a down clue

parts.note: sweet FA, or FA, is slang for nothing at all, like not a sausage
a ford is a place to cross a river

explanation.surface: An irritated reply when someone offers nothing in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns FA into AF. 'Not a sausage' is British slang for nothing; so is 'sweet FA'.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford someone an opportunity is to give or provide it, a synonym for offer.

clue.text: Was sacked after fake election? Flipping rubbish!

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters behind the fake piece

parts.note: cod means sham or mock, as in cod Latin

indicators.note: sacked, as in a city plundered, throws the letters about
flipping turns the election word over, reading it backwards

parts.note: a poll is an election

explanation.surface: An outraged cry that someone was fired after a rigged vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges the first word and 'Flipping' turns the election word round, though it looks like a mild British oath. Cod means sham, as in cod Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word for nonsense means the same as rubbish.

clue.text: Take off perch breaking foot

indicators.note: breaking into a word puts the perch word inside it

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay
a perch, or rod, is an old unit of length of five and a half yards

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a bird from its roost, which then breaks a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: A perch and a rod are both the same old measure; 'foot' looks like another unit but means pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them for comic effect, which is what a send-up does.

clue.text: Catch fellows and female cycling separately

indicators.note: cycling sends letters round from one end of the fellows word to the other

parts.note: men are fellows

indicators.note: separately says the female word is cycled on its own too

parts.note: she denotes a female

explanation.surface: Men and a woman go cycling apart and get caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' turns MEN into ENM, and 'separately' cycles SHE into ESH on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle something in a net is to trap or snare it.

clue.text: Accommodating mates on the dole?

parts.note: pals who are obliging in bed, read literally as chums drawing state welfare

explanation.surface: A question about whether one's out-of-work pals are helpful hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the dole' is British for receiving unemployment benefit; 'accommodating' hints at a casual sexual arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names companions who share casual sex without romance, read literally as pals receiving welfare.

clue.text: Threatened beastly islander during third night back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
during says the letters lie within the words third night

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A savage islander made threats during the third night of the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'during' in the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, so the definition ends at 'islander'. The indri is an endangered lemur of Madagascar.
explanation.definitionFit: This large lemur lives only on Madagascar and is critically endangered, an island animal under threat.

clue.text: 7 possibly green? It's unlikely

indicators.note: an unlikely form of the letters is a rearranged one

parts.note: taken as written, the 's adding no letter

explanation.surface: Could the number seven be green? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' rearranges GREEN and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a whole number, so it is an example of one; 'possibly' marks it as an example.

clue.text: French river understood to have drowned Resistance

indicators.note: to have drowned something is to have it submerged within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: I see means I understand
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A French river where Resistance fighters were drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside I SEE. The capital in 'Resistance' evokes the wartime French Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: This river of south-east France flows from the Alps into the Rhône.

clue.text: Glider op deployed energy beam

indicators.note: deployed troops are spread out in new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A glider operation is launched, powered by an energy beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges GLIDER OP into RIDGEPOL.
explanation.definitionFit: This horizontal timber along the top of a roof is a structural beam.

clue.text: Passed with top marks Trump originally claimed … or pretended

indicators.note: claimed, as in captured, holds the letter inside the other word

parts.note: to ace an exam is to pass it brilliantly

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of Trump

explanation.surface: Trump claimed he passed with flying colours, or was he putting it on?
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside ACED; 'claimed' looks like said but means took in.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a part or feigning is a synonym for putting on a show.

clue.text: See 22
